DataStandardEnum.name: DataStandardEnum
DataStandardEnum.description:
Data standards and common data models a dataset's content follows.
Deliberately **not** merged into `FormatEnum` (#403). A serialization and a data standard are different concepts: CSV says how bytes are laid out, OMOP CDM says what the columns mean. Widening `FormatEnum` to absorb DICOM would conflate them and make `format` unanswerable.
Free-text `conforms_to` records what a source *says*; this records which registered standard that is, where one applies. Both may be populated for the same standard — one verbatim, one normalized — which is the ordinary label-plus-code pattern and is consistent with the per-slot completeness decision on #501.
⚠️ **No `meaning:` is asserted on any value.** Several of these standards have no stable ontology term this repository can verify, and inventing a CURIE that resolves to nothing is worse than leaving the grounding absent — it is the exact failure `d4d runs identifiers` exists to find. A declared standards-registry prefix is the natural home for these once such a registry carries them; until one does, this is a controlled vocabulary without ontology grounding, and says so.

DICOM.description: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine — imaging data and its acquisition metadata.

BIDS.description: Brain Imaging Data Structure — a file and directory layout with accompanying metadata for neuroimaging and related recordings.

OMOP_CDM.description: Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model — a relational model for observational health data.

WFDB.description: WaveForm DataBase — physiologic signal records and annotations.

OPEN_MHEALTH.description: Open mHealth — schemas for mobile health and wearable measures.

ESDS.description: ASCII File Format Guidelines for Earth Science Data.

RO_CRATE.description: RO-Crate — a packaging convention describing a dataset and its context as linked data.

FHIR.description: HL7 FHIR — a standard for exchanging healthcare information.

OTHER.description: A standard the sources name that has no value here. Use it **with** `conforms_to` carrying the name as the source states it, so the fact is not lost to the absence of a term. A run must never pick a near-neighbour: reporting BIDS because a dataset is neuroimaging, when the sources say something else, is an invention.

BiasTypeEnum.name: BiasTypeEnum
BiasTypeEnum.description: Types of bias that may be present in datasets. Values are mapped to the Artificial Intelligence Ontology (AIO) bias taxonomy from BioPortal. See https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/AIO

selection_bias.description: Bias arising from non-random selection of data or participants.

measurement_bias.description: Bias in how data is measured or recorded. Occurs when features and labels are proxies for desired quantities, potentially leading to differential performance.

historical_bias.description: Bias reflecting historical inequities or societal biases. Long-standing biases encoded in society over time.

representation_bias.description: Certain groups are over- or under-represented in the data. Results from non-random sampling of subgroups making trends non-generalizable to new populations.

aggregation_bias.description: Bias from inappropriately combining distinct groups. Related to making inferences about individuals based on their group membership.

algorithmic_bias.description: Bias introduced or amplified by algorithmic processing. Computational bias from data analysis processes and methods.

sampling_bias.description: Bias from sampling methodology not representative of the population.

annotation_bias.description: Bias introduced during data labeling or annotation. Occurs when annotators rely on heuristics or exhibit systematic patterns in labeling.

confirmation_bias.description: Bias from seeking data that confirms pre-existing beliefs. Tendency to prefer information that confirms existing beliefs, influencing the search for, interpretation of, and recall of information.

LimitationTypeEnum.name: LimitationTypeEnum
LimitationTypeEnum.description: Types of limitations that may affect dataset use or interpretation. Distinct from biases (systematic errors) and anomalies (data quality issues).

scope_limitation.description: Dataset does not cover all intended use cases or populations. The scope of the dataset is narrower than the intended application domain.

temporal_limitation.description: Dataset is limited to specific time periods. Data may not reflect current conditions or may not be applicable to other time periods.

coverage_limitation.description: Dataset has incomplete coverage of target domain. Missing data points, categories, or geographic regions within the intended scope.

methodological_limitation.description: Data collection methodology introduces constraints. Limitations arising from how data was gathered, measured, or processed.

representativeness_limitation.description: Dataset may not be representative of target population. Sample may not accurately reflect the broader population of interest.

resolution_limitation.description: Data granularity or resolution is insufficient for some uses. Level of detail may not support fine-grained analysis or specific applications.

integration_limitation.description: Challenges in combining with other data sources. Incompatibilities in formats, identifiers, or schemas that hinder data integration.

DatasetRelationshipTypeEnum.name: DatasetRelationshipTypeEnum
DatasetRelationshipTypeEnum.description:
Relationships between datasets, aligned one-to-one with the DataCite Metadata Schema RelationType controlled vocabulary and mapped to Dublin Core terms where an equivalent exists.
Permissible value names are snake_case, following this schema's naming throughout. The corresponding DataCite term is carried in `aliases` on each value, so the alignment is machine-readable rather than asserted in prose. DataCite publishes no per-term IRIs, which is why the link is an alias and not a `meaning`.
All 36 DataCite RelationType values are represented. Generators reading DataCite metadata should map the CamelCase term to the snake_case name via `aliases`; emitting the DataCite spelling directly will not validate.
See https://datacite-metadata-schema.readthedocs.io/ and http://purl.org/dc/terms/

ComplianceStatusEnum.name: ComplianceStatusEnum
ComplianceStatusEnum.description: Compliance status for regulatory frameworks. Indicates the extent to which a dataset complies with specific regulations (e.g., HIPAA, 45 CFR 46). These are workflow status values that may evolve as regulations are assessed or as the dataset is modified.

compliant.description: Dataset is compliant with the regulation. All requirements are met and documented.

partially_compliant.description: Dataset is partially compliant, with known limitations or gaps in compliance. Some but not all requirements are met.

not_compliant.description: Dataset does not comply with the regulation. Significant requirements are not met.

not_applicable.description: Regulation does not apply to this dataset based on scope, jurisdiction, or subject matter.

under_review.description: Compliance status is currently under review or assessment. Final determination has not been made.

ConfidentialityLevelEnum.name: ConfidentialityLevelEnum
ConfidentialityLevelEnum.description:
Confidentiality classification levels for datasets indicating the degree of access restrictions and data sensitivity.
NOTE: This enum classifies data sensitivity and access control (WHO can access), which is orthogonal to DataUsePermissionEnum that specifies use restrictions (WHAT authorized users can do with data). ConfidentialityLevelEnum determines access requirements, while DataUsePermissionEnum uses DUO terms to specify permitted uses once access is granted.

unrestricted.description: No confidentiality restrictions. Data is publicly available with no access controls required. Equivalent to public or open access data.

restricted.description: Restricted access requiring approval or registration. Data contains sensitive information requiring controlled access. May require account creation, data use agreement, or institutional approval.

confidential.description: Highly confidential with strict access controls. Data contains highly sensitive information with significant privacy or security implications. Typically requires IRB approval, formal data use agreements, institutional authorization, or other formal vetting processes.

DataUsePermissionEnum.name: DataUsePermissionEnum
DataUsePermissionEnum.description: Data use permissions and restrictions based on the Data Use Ontology (DUO). DUO is a standardized ontology for representing data use conditions developed by GA4GH. See https://github.com/EBISPOT/DUO

general_research_use.description: Data available for any research purpose (GRU).

health_medical_biomedical_research.description: Data limited to health, medical, or biomedical research (HMB).

disease_specific_research.description: Data limited to research on specified disease(s) (DS).

population_origins_ancestry_research.description: Data limited to population origins or ancestry research (POA).

clinical_care_use.description: Data available for clinical care and applications (CC).

no_commercial_use.description: Data use limited to non-commercial purposes (NCU).

non_profit_use_only.description: Data use limited to not-for-profit organizations (NPU).

non_profit_use_and_non_commercial_use.description: Data limited to not-for-profit organizations and non-commercial use (NPUNCU).

no_methods_development.description: Data cannot be used for methods or software development (NMDS).

genetic_studies_only.description: Data limited to genetic studies only (GSO).

ethics_approval_required.description: Ethics approval (e.g., IRB/ERB) required for data use (IRB).

publication_required.description: Results must be published/shared with research community (PUB).

geographic_restriction.description: Data use limited to specific geographic region (GS).

institution_specific.description: Data use limited to approved institutions (IS).

project_specific.description: Data use limited to approved project(s) (PS).

user_specific.description: Data use limited to approved users (US).

time_limit.description: Data use approved for limited time period (TS).

return_to_database.description: Derived data must be returned to database/resource (RTN).

VariableTypeEnum.description: Common data types for variables. Values are mapped to schema.org DataType vocabulary. See https://schema.org/DataType

ordinal.description: Ordered categorical variables where values have a meaningful sequence (e.g., low/medium/high, strongly disagree/disagree/agree/strongly agree).

array.description: Arrays or lists of values. May contain elements of the same or different types.

object.description: Complex structured objects or nested data structures.

⚠️ **No `meaning:` is asserted on any value.** Several of these standards have no stable ontology term this repository can verify, and inventing a CURIE that resolves to nothing is worse than leaving the grounding absent — it is the exact failure `d4d runs identifiers` exists to find. A declared standards-registry prefix is the natural home for these once such a registry carries them; until one does, this is a controlled vocabulary without ontology grounding, and says so.

All 36 DataCite RelationType values are represented. Generators reading DataCite metadata should map the CamelCase term to the snake_case name via `aliases`; emitting the DataCite spelling directly will not validate.
See https://datacite-metadata-schema.readthedocs.io/ and http://purl.org/dc/terms/

Distinct from `compensation_type` and `compensation_amount`, which record what was provided. State this only where a source describes the structure. An escalating payment schedule is not by itself evidence that retention was its purpose; report the schedule under the compensation slots and leave this absent.
⚠️ **"Retention" here means keeping participants enrolled, never keeping data.** How long the data is kept belongs in `retention_limit`, which is a different slot about a different subject. The word is treacherous in this corpus: across all five project bundles nearly every occurrence of "retention" is about data or specimen retention — "limits on the retention of the data", "bioSpecRetention", "records retention requirements" — and none so far describes an incentive structure. An empty slot is the correct outcome for those sources.

d4d_generation_record.yaml/GenerationRec.description: Names the kind of file. Not always `d4d_generation_provenance`, as this said before it was checked: a derived record writes `d4d_derived_provenance`, and calling both by one name would hide the distinction the mode exists to draw.
Bumped when the record's shape changes incompatibly. Still 1: every block added since has been additive, which is why records written months apart still validate together.

How much of this record is observed. `live` is written by the run itself; `reconstructed` is assembled afterwards and names what it cannot recover; `derived` describes a record computed from other records rather than generated.
When the record was written, not when the run started.
Which project, method, label and arm this run is.
The schema the run generated against, by hash and by digest. The digest is what the model was actually sent.
The commit the run was made at.
Versions of the packages that produced the record.

The records this run wrote, by path and size — **not** by hash for a generation record. `_artifact` drops the hash deliberately: the agent path records provenance as a separate step from writing the artifacts, so 77 live records had hashed a state their files merely passed through. Integrity lives in `validation.artifacts`, computed after the run is final. A *derived* record does hash its outputs, because it writes and hashes them in one step.
The bundle the run consumed, its hash, and the manifest that selected it. Absent on a `derived` record, which consumes records rather than a bundle.
Model, provider, route, per-phase ceilings, and what can honestly be said about temperature, reasoning effort and context.
The machine the run was made on.
Every prompt file the run consumed, hashed, plus the assembly digest covering the phase instructions and their order.
The instruction files an agentic run opens for itself, hashed. Carries `consumed`, which says whether this runtime reads them at all.

Everything else a reader may need, by reference rather than by copy: the reasoning log beside this record, the registries the run was checked against, and the telemetry report derived from records like it. A registry is shared and appended to over time, so copying it into every record would multiply it and still not say which version was in force; a hash does say.
One entry per API call: phase, attempt, timing, tokens and stop reason. Absent for a runtime with no access to its own accounting.
What an agentic run says about the phases it performed. The counterpart to `api_usage` for a runtime that knows which phase it ran but not what the call cost.
Phases a resumed run did not repeat.

Present when the core record was derived from the audited full record rather than generated (#694): the rule, the full record's path and md5 it was projected from, the identity-slot count and projection list, and the slots deliberately not derived. A run carrying this block made no `core`, `reconcile_core` or `repair_core` model call; its api_usage has no such phases and that is not a gap.
Registered receipt-only continuation with immutable input/request/response/result pins, v4 accounting and independent coverage policy (#4266).
Optional registered shared-generation API execution identity and reconstructed typed-audit declaration; absent on historical/default runs (#4345,
Opt-in restore-only policy, admitted attempt and mechanically checked final outcome (#2923).
Current removals reading for the explicit restore-only policy; absent on historical records.
Validator-driven repair rounds, in order.

Present when repair rewrote a record after the reconciliation report was written, naming which records changed and why the report was regenerated (#604). Absent on the ordinary path, where the report already describes the final bytes.
Missing from the first version of this schema, and found by the conformance gate on its first run rather than by inspection: no record on disk carries it, so validating the corpus could not have reached it. That is the difference the gate makes — it checks the writers, not the archive.
Exactly one other attribute is in the same position: `companions`, which `build_record` writes unconditionally and which will appear on the next record written. Named here because presenting this field as the single thing the gate surfaced would overstate a real result by leaving out its twin (#618).
Phase snapshots written as the run progressed.
Whether the records validate, pinned to the bytes and the schema the verdict was reached on, so a stale verdict is detectable.
Whether the full and core records agree. A property of two files together, which no single-file gate can see.
Whether the reconciliation report's claims survive checking against the record and the schema.

What the write-time normalisers changed: identifier rewrites (#974) and mailto ids (#981) by phase and slot with occurrence and distinct-value counts, and British spellings rewritten to American (#1002: `british_spellings` by phase and slot, `british_occurrences`, `british_distinct`, `british_skipped` for the title-case runs and genus names left as written) — so the record says what the model wrote although the record as written carries none of it.

What the in-process report check found before the run completed (#929, v8 step E): claims checked and contradictions before, whether the report was regenerated once with the contradictions named, and what remained after. Includes `report_audit_totals` findings when `findings_include_report_audit_totals: true` (#4766). The final `report_claims` and `report_audit_totals` blocks are recomputed from the report as it stands.
Deterministic check comparing written report's stated finding total and per-severity subtotals against structured audit counts (#4766).

Counts that are properties of the records alone — undeclared CURIE prefixes, British spellings in generated prose, and fragments on organisational identifiers. Separate from `grounding` because they need no bundle: burying them there would make three preregistered predictions unmeasurable for every record whose bundle has drifted.
Whether external identifiers appear in the bundle they were read from, and whether identifier slots hold resolver URLs.

The coverage receipt checked against the chunk manifest, the bundle and the full record (#708): chunks reviewed N/N, snippets verified M/M, slots with a receipt S/T, findings, and the non-checks named. `expected` says whether the run's procedure wrote one; an expected receipt that could not be checked is unmeasurable, not clean.

A canary verdict recorded on the run: status (ok / regressed / unmeasurable), the metric rows against the baseline, a basis saying when and from what it was computed, and recorded_by naming who. Written by `d4d api batch` at the gate since #1020 (the verdict it acted on, `recorded_by: d4d api batch`) and offline by `d4d api verdict` when a verdict is re-derived after a checker revision (#877, #892, #1030), the prior block kept whole under `prior_verdict` with its own `recorded_at`/`recorded_by`.

A reviewer's answers to the record's review pack (#787), checked: items answered N/N, adverse verdicts, cannot_tell, findings, and the reviewer's identity. The judgement half of the receipt design — what the deterministic validator cannot decide — as a recorded artifact.

Curator dispositions of review-pass findings on this record (#903), in order: each names the review item, the disposition — `retain` (documented and left as generated) or `amend` (one literal replacement applied to the full record and, where it carries the text, the core record, with both files' sha256 before and after) — the note, and who and when. Written by `d4d review disposition --execute`; nothing else writes it. An amendment is a curator act on a generated record and is its own definition; evaluations made before it are named as predating it, never re-attributed.
Values recorded but not observed. Named rather than silently trusted.
Fields a reconstructed record cannot establish, with the reason. The difference between a gap that is named and one that is hidden.
Free-text observations about this run.
For a `derived` record: how it was computed from other records.
For a `derived` record: the records it consumed, hashed.
Fields that do not apply to this kind of record, with the reason — distinct from a field that is missing.
For a canonicalised record: what it was canonicalised from.
The record that replaced this one, if any.

Every `canonical` block this record once carried, newest first, each with the pointer that displaced it (#677). Demoted rather than deleted, so the displaced selection's evidence — criterion, candidates, margin — stays in the live corpus.

**When it was computed differs by runtime**, and the two are not the same claim. The API path fingerprints the digest as it renders it to send, so the value is of the bytes the model received. d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetryRepor.description: The run label the report covers, e.g. 2026-08-05_claude-opus-5-1m-generic-v3.
Version of this telemetry schema the report conforms to.
Every run found under the label, one entry per project.
Mechanical cross-run comparisons, one per metric, computed by the collector — no judgement, only numbers set side by side.
Authored analysis: observations, comparisons and interpretations, each labeled with how much judgement it carries.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/proj.description: Project the run documents, e.g. AI_READI.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/repl.description: Replicate number parsed from the run label.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/labe.description: Full run label including the replicate suffix.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/mode.description: Model route the run was billed against, as recorded.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/prov.description: API provider, e.g. LBL CBORG (proxy to Anthropic).

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/arm.description: Experimental arm, e.g. BASELINE (input documents only).

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/vali.description: Final validation outcome of both records.
How many artifacts still carry validation problems.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/timi.description: Where every time figure in this run comes from.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/wall.description: Coarse whole-run estimate; basis given by timing_basis. Absent when no two time points exist to subtract.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/tota.description: Sum of uncached input tokens across every billed call.
Sum of output tokens (thinking and visible text together).
Sum of prompt-cache read tokens across every billed call.
Sum of prompt-cache write tokens across every billed call.

Sum of per-attempt estimates (output tokens minus a chars/4 estimate of visible text). Sound for comparison, not cost attribution. The requests name no thinking display, so on the Opus 5 family, whose default display is omitted, their thinking text is empty and this estimate is the measure this report carries (#2542, #2622, #2669).

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/appr.description: input*$5/M + cache_write*$6.25/M + cache_read*$0.50/M + output*$25/M at the CBORG-posted opus-5 rates; an estimate, not an invoice.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/invo.description: How many batch invocations the run took. Completed-but-invalid runs keep resume state so a re-run can continue repair (#361, #362), so more than one is routine for large records.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/reco.description: File and content statistics of the run's final artifacts.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/pres.description: Field-presence rubric scores whose recorded path matches this run's artifacts. Empty until the presence evaluator is run against this label's files (#286).

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/llm_.description: LLM-as-judge rubric scores whose recorded path matches this run's artifacts. Empty until the judge is run against this label's files.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/phas.description: Per-phase attempt history, in first-appearance order.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RunTelemetry/repa.description: Validator-driven repair rounds with their outcomes.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/PhaseTelemetry/ph.description: Which phase these attempts belong to.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/PhaseTelemetry/at.description: Every billed attempt of this phase, in call order.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/PhaseTelemetry/ar.description: Modification time of the artifact this phase writes, when the file still exists. The only per-phase time point for runs predating recorded timing.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/AttemptTelemetry/.description: Attempt number as recorded; numbers repeat across invocations while list order is chronological.
Present only for runs made after timing was recorded.
Wall time of the call, retries at the transport layer included.
Uncached input tokens billed for this call.
Prompt-cache tokens read by this call.
Prompt-cache tokens written by this call.
The ceiling requested, after the per-route clamp.
Why the model stopped on this attempt.
Output tokens minus a chars/4 estimate of visible text.
A thinking block came back, whether or not it carried text.
The thinking text itself was capturable, not just attested.

Why an attempt was abandoned (a stream that ended without message_stop, a transport error) — present only on rows that made no completed call (#1017); a sweep's dropped-stream count is the number of attempts carrying one.
Why the runner refused a billed reply whose body it kept (#1048); the attempt is otherwise indistinguishable from the one accepted, and the report's comparisons pass over it (#2892, #2903).

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RecordStats/artif.description: Which artifact this describes — full, core or report.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RecordStats/path.description: Repository-relative path of the file measured.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RecordStats/sha25.description: Hash of the measured bytes, pinning what was described.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RecordStats/root_.description: Top-level keys the parsed record carries.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RecordStats/popul.description: Top-level keys whose value is not hollow — hollow being null, a blank string, an empty container, or a container whose every member is hollow, recursively.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RecordStats/hollo.description: Maximal hollow subtrees at any depth: a hollow object counts once, not once per empty member. The mechanical, structural kin of the form-defects hollow_object class, which is LLM-judged.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Comparison/metric.description: What is being compared, e.g. full_phase_output_tokens.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Comparison/unit.description: Unit of the values, e.g. tokens, USD, slots, rounds.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/ComparisonValue/s.description: The run measured, e.g. AI_READI rep1.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/EvaluationScore/r.description: Which rubric produced the score, e.g. rubric10, rubric20.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/EvaluationScore/a.description: Which of the run's artifacts was scored — full or core.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/EvaluationScore/j.description: The judging model, for llm_judge evaluations.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/EvaluationScore/e.description: When the evaluation ran, as recorded by the evaluator.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/EvaluationScore/s.description: Path of the evaluation output the score was read from.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Finding/topic.description: Short subject line, e.g. repair convergence.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Finding/kind.description: How much judgement the claim carries.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Finding/claim.description: The statement itself, one or two sentences.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Finding/evidence.description: What backs the claim — figures, file paths, issue numbers. A finding without evidence is an opinion and should say so via kind.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/Finding/relates_t.description: Related run labels, projects or issue references.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RepairRound/round.description: Repair round number within one invocation.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RepairRound/outco.description: applied, truncated, unusable response, not converging, or validator did not run.

d4d_run_telemetry.yaml/RepairRound/findi.description: Validator finding lines this round started from.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/file_col.description: Collection of file groups within this dataset. Each entry represents a logical grouping of files with shared characteristics (e.g., all training data, all image files, all raw data files). Maps to nested RO-Crate Dataset entities via schema:hasPart in RO-Crate converters.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/total_fi.description: Total number of files across all file collections in this dataset. Can be aggregated from file_collections[].file_count.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/total_si.description: Total size of all files in bytes across all file collections. Can be aggregated from file_collections[].total_bytes.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/purposes.description: Purposes for which the dataset was created. List of Purpose objects from the Motivation module, each describing a specific creation goal or intended application.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/tasks.description: Tasks the dataset is intended to support. List of Task objects from the Motivation module describing specific machine learning, research, or analytical tasks.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/addressi.description: Research or practical gaps this dataset addresses. List of AddressingGap objects from the Motivation module, each describing a gap in existing datasets or knowledge that this dataset fills.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/creators.description: Individuals or organizations who created the dataset. List of Creator objects describing authorship, roles, and affiliations of dataset creators.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/funders.description: Funding mechanisms that supported dataset creation. List of FundingMechanism objects describing grants, contracts, or other funding sources including grantors and grant identifiers.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/subsets.description: Subsets or splits of this dataset. List of DataSubset objects from the Composition module, each representing a logical partition such as training, validation, or test splits, or demographic subgroups.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/instance.description: Individual data instances or records in the dataset. List of Instance objects from the Composition module describing what each data point represents, its type, and associated label information.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/anomalie.description: Known data quality issues, errors, or irregularities in the dataset. List of DataAnomaly objects from the Composition module, each documenting a specific anomaly and its potential impact.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/known_bi.description: List of known biases present in the dataset that may affect fairness, representativeness, or model performance. Uses BiasTypeEnum for standardized bias categorization mapped to the AI Ontology (AIO).

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/known_li.description: List of known limitations of the dataset that may affect its use or interpretation. Distinct from biases (systematic errors) and anomalies (data quality issues).

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/confiden.description: Confidential or restricted information within the dataset that requires access controls. List of Confidentiality objects describing what is confidential and why it cannot be released.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/content_.description: Content warnings for potentially harmful, offensive, or disturbing material in the dataset. List of ContentWarning objects alerting users to sensitive content categories.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/subpopul.description: Subpopulations represented within the dataset. List of Subpopulation objects from the Composition module describing demographic or other groups, their representation, and any imbalances.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/sensitiv.description: Sensitive data elements requiring special handling or access controls. List of SensitiveElement objects identifying sensitive attributes such as personal identifiers, protected health information, or legally sensitive content.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/relation.description: Explicit relationships between individual instances in the dataset. List of Relationships objects from the Composition module describing how instances relate (e.g., graph edges, ratings, social network links).

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/splits.description: Recommended data splits for this dataset. List of Splits objects from the Composition module describing train/validation/test partitions and the rationale for each split strategy.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/acquisit.description: Methods used to acquire or obtain dataset instances. List of InstanceAcquisition objects from the Collection module describing how data was sourced, whether directly observed or derived.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/collecti.description: Mechanisms, instruments, or tools used for data collection. List of CollectionMechanism objects from the Collection module describing sensors, surveys, APIs, or other collection instruments.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/sampling.description: Strategies used to select data instances from a larger population. List of SamplingStrategy objects from the Collection module describing sampling methodology, inclusion criteria, and limitations.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/data_col.description: Individuals or organizations responsible for collecting the data. List of DataCollector objects from the Collection module describing who performed data collection and their roles.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/collecti.description: Time periods during which data was collected. List of CollectionTimeframe objects from the Collection module describing collection start and end dates, and any gaps in the collection period.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/direct_c.description: Whether data was collected directly from individuals or via third parties. List of DirectCollection objects from the Collection module describing direct vs. indirect collection methods and sources.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/collecti.description: Notifications provided to individuals about data collection. List of CollectionNotification objects from the Ethics module describing how and when individuals were informed about the data collection.
Consent obtained from individuals for data collection and use. List of CollectionConsent objects from the Ethics module describing how consent was requested, provided, and documented.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/consent_.description: Mechanisms for individuals to revoke previously given consent. List of ConsentRevocation objects from the Ethics module describing how revocation works and what happens to data after revocation.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/missing_.description: One or more records documenting missing data patterns and handling strategies.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/raw_data.description: List of raw data sources before preprocessing. Each RawDataSource object describes where the original data came from and how it can be accessed.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/ethical_.description: Ethical reviews and institutional oversight for the dataset. List of EthicalReview objects from the Ethics module describing IRB approvals, ethics committee reviews, and compliance certifications.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/data_pro.description: Data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) conducted for the dataset. List of DataProtectionImpact objects from the Ethics module documenting privacy risk assessments and mitigation measures.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/human_su.description: Information about whether dataset involves human subjects research, including IRB approval, ethics review, and regulatory compliance.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/informed.description: One or more records detailing informed consent procedures, including consent type, documentation, and withdrawal mechanisms.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/at_risk_.description: Information about protections for at-risk populations (e.g., minors, pregnant women, prisoners) including special safeguards and assent procedures.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/particip.description: One or more records describing privacy protections and anonymization procedures for human research participants.
One or more records describing compensation or incentives provided to human research participants.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/preproce.description: Preprocessing steps applied to the raw data. List of PreprocessingStrategy objects from the Preprocessing module describing normalization, transformation, and other preparation steps.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/cleaning.description: Data cleaning and quality control procedures applied to the dataset. List of CleaningStrategy objects from the Preprocessing module describing outlier removal, deduplication, and error correction steps.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/labeling.description: Labeling or annotation methodologies applied to the data. List of LabelingStrategy objects from the Preprocessing module describing annotation procedures, annotator qualifications, and quality controls.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/raw_sour.description: Raw, unprocessed source data before any preprocessing was applied. List of RawData objects from the Preprocessing module describing original data sources and their formats.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/imputati.description: Data imputation protocols applied to handle missing values. List of ImputationProtocol objects from the Preprocessing module describing the imputation technique, affected variables, and rationale.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/annotati.description: One or more analyses of annotation quality and inter-annotator agreement.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/machine_.description: List of automated annotation tools used in dataset creation.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/existing.description: Known existing uses of the dataset at the time of publication. List of ExistingUse objects from the Uses module describing research, commercial, or other applications of the dataset.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/use_repo.description: Repositories or registries tracking how the dataset has been used. List of UseRepository objects from the Uses module pointing to papers with code, citation indices, or other use-tracking resources.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/other_ta.description: Additional tasks the dataset may support beyond its original intent. List of OtherTask objects from the Uses module describing potential applications not originally planned by the dataset creators.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/future_u.description: Anticipated impacts of future uses, including risks and benefits. List of FutureUseImpact objects from the Uses module describing foreseeable consequences of using this dataset in new applications.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/discoura.description: Uses that are not recommended for this dataset due to limitations, risks, or ethical concerns. List of DiscouragedUse objects from the Uses module explaining why certain applications should be avoided.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/intended.description: List of explicit intended and recommended uses for this dataset. Complements future_use_impacts by focusing on positive applications.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/prohibit.description: List of explicitly prohibited or forbidden uses for this dataset. Stronger than discouraged_uses - these are not permitted.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/distribu.description: Formats in which the dataset is distributed or made available. List of DistributionFormat objects from the Distribution module describing file formats, compression, and access methods.

Dates when the dataset was or will be distributed or released. List of DistributionDate objects from the Distribution module describing initial release dates, version release dates, and planned future releases.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/third_pa.description: Third-party distribution policies for the dataset. List of ThirdPartySharing objects from the Distribution module describing whether and how the dataset is shared with entities outside the creating organization.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/license_.description: License and usage terms governing dataset access and use. LicenseAndUseTerms object from the Data Governance module describing the applicable license, permitted uses, and any restrictions.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/ip_restr.description: Intellectual property restrictions on dataset use or redistribution. IPRestrictions object from the Data Governance module describing copyright, trademark, or other IP considerations.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/regulato.description: Regulatory and export control restrictions applicable to the dataset. ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions object from the Data Governance module describing compliance requirements such as ITAR, EAR, or GDPR.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/data_gov.description:
Who decides who may use this dataset, and how. DataGovernance object from the Data Governance module describing the access committee, its membership and contacts, the review process, and who remains accountable for the data over time.
Distinct from `license_and_use_terms` (the terms) and `regulatory_restrictions` (the regulations): this is the people and the process that apply them. Added because `Dataset` previously had no governance slot at all, so a data access committee could only be named by nesting its chair inside an export-control statement (#503).

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/maintain.description: Individuals or organizations responsible for maintaining the dataset. List of Maintainer objects from the Maintenance module describing maintenance contacts, roles, and support channels.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/errata.description: Known errors or corrections to the dataset since publication. List of Erratum objects from the Maintenance module describing discovered errors, affected records, and correction procedures.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/updates.description: Plans for future updates or versioning of the dataset. UpdatePlan object from the Maintenance module describing update frequency, versioning policy, and planned enhancements.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/retentio.description: Data retention policies and limits for the dataset. RetentionLimits object from the Maintenance module describing how long the dataset will be available and any deletion schedules.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/version_.description: Information about access to different versions of the dataset. VersionAccess object from the Maintenance module describing where older versions can be found and how version history is maintained.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/extensio.description: Mechanisms for extending or contributing to the dataset. ExtensionMechanism object from the Maintenance module describing how others can propose additions, corrections, or expansions.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/variable.description: List of metadata records describing individual variables, fields, or columns in the dataset.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/is_deide.description: De-identification status and procedures applied to the dataset. Deidentification object describing whether the dataset contains personal data, what de-identification methods were applied, and any residual re-identification risks.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/is_tabul.description: Whether the dataset is in tabular format (rows and columns). True if the data is structured as a table (e.g., CSV, TSV, relational database); false for unstructured formats such as images or free text.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/citation.description: Recommended citation for this dataset in DataCite or BibTeX format. Provides a standard way to cite the dataset in publications.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/parent_d.description: One or more parent datasets that this dataset is part of or derived from. Enables hierarchical dataset composition (hasPart/isPartOf relationships).

data_sheets_schema.yaml/Dataset/related_.description: List of related datasets with typed relationships (e.g., supplements, derives from, is version of). Use DatasetRelationship class to specify relationship types.

data_sheets_schema.yaml/DataSubset/is_da.description: Is this subset a split of the larger dataset, e.g., is it a set for model training, testing, or validation?

data_sheets_schema.yaml/DataSubset/is_su.description: Is this subset a subpopulation of the larger dataset, e.g., is it a set of data for a specific demographic?

publication_redaction.method: Email-address strings are redacted after counts, original-byte hashes and equality comparisons are computed. Recorded hashes and byte lengths refer to the original inputs, not redacted response text.
